Read a dataset

Source: R/read.R
store_read.Rd

Reads a table, a geospatial dataset or a raster from a store. Filters and column selection are pushed into the scan, so only the needed files, row groups and columns are read.

Usage

store_read(
  st,
  dataset,
  ...,
  columns = NULL,
  intersects = NULL,
  geometry = TRUE,
  version = NULL,
  copy = NULL,
  exact = TRUE,
  exact_engine = NULL
)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

dataset

Name of the dataset: the full name, or its last part when that is unique in the store.

...

Filter expressions, as in dplyr::filter().

columns

Columns to return, as in dplyr::select() (tidyselect); NULL for all. The geometry column is controlled by geometry. A raster has no column selection.

intersects

NULL, or a query: an sf, sfc or bbox object with a coordinate reference system, or H3 cells of any resolution as hex strings, bit64::integer64 or h3o H3 vectors. A plain number aborts: it cannot hold an H3 cell. An sf or sfc query with an invalid geometry (for example a ring that crosses itself) aborts, with the reason and advice to use sf::st_make_valid(); validity is read on the sphere or in the plane as in store_intersects(). For a raster, the query's bounding box is the window that is read (see "Rasters").

geometry

FALSE drops the geometry before reading and returns a tibble.

version

NULL for the current version, or the 16 hex characters of an earlier version kept in the history.

copy

Whether to copy the dataset to the local secondary locations before reading (see "Copy to secondary locations"). NULL (the default) copies the current version when the connection's copy_on_read is TRUE and the bytes to download are at or under the limit. TRUE copies whatever the limit and the connection's setting, and copies an earlier version too, into the secondaries' history. FALSE never copies.

exact

TRUE tests the candidate rows of a spatial filter exactly, on the sphere or in the plane as exact_engine says.

exact_engine

How the exact test of a spatial filter reads the geometries: NULL (the default) follows the geocoding engine the dataset was written with ("s2": on the sphere; "planar": in the plane; "auto": on the sphere for rows valid on the sphere, in the plane for the others), and the session's sf::sf_use_s2() setting for a dataset with no recorded engine (written before engines were recorded, or with geocode = FALSE). "s2", "planar" or "session" override it. Data in a projected CRS are always tested in the plane of that CRS. See store_intersects().

Value

A tibble; an sf object for geospatial data read with geometry; a terra::SpatRaster for a raster, with the categories and the colours recorded when it was written.

Details

  • Filters (...) are dplyr filter expressions. A filter whose columns are all partition columns is first evaluated on the partition values in the catalog, so only the files of the matching partitions are opened.

  • intersects keeps the rows of a geospatial dataset whose geometry intersects a query shape or H3 cells (see store_intersects() for the steps). With exact = FALSE or geometry = FALSE the result is the candidate set, a superset of the intersecting rows, and a message says so.

  • A geospatial dataset is returned as an sf object with the catalog's coordinate reference system, or as a tibble with geometry = FALSE. Of the columns the package adds, the row identifier .rcs_id is dropped (unless named in columns); the H3 cell h3 (bit64::integer64, see store_h3_hex()), the bounding box bbox and the partition column h3_p<r> are returned.

  • A raster is returned as a terra::SpatRaster opened through GDAL, so only the tiles needed are read; intersects crops it to the query's bounding box (see "Rasters"). Filters, columns, geometry, exact and exact_engine do not apply to rasters and abort.

Rasters

A raster is returned as a terra::SpatRaster that points to the stored file: at the location itself for a local store, through GDAL's virtual file system for a bucket. No cell is read until it is needed: GDAL fetches only the tiles a calculation or a window needs, from the location read from. The file itself is copied only by a copy to a secondary location (below).

A raster is one file, so copying it to a secondary location is all or nothing (see "Copy to secondary locations"). With a primary in a bucket and a local secondary that lacks the raster or holds an older version, the whole file is first copied to the secondary when it is at or under the size limit, and the raster, or its window, is then read from that copy. With copy = FALSE, a connection made with copy_on_read = FALSE, or a file above the limit, nothing is copied and the read stays on the bucket.

  • The whole raster. store_read(st, "name") returns every layer, with the layer names, the data type and the NoData value of the file. Cells that hold the NoData value are missing (NA).

  • A window. intersects returns only the part inside the bounding box of the query, in the raster's CRS, rounded outwards to whole cells; a point or a line gives the cells it touches. The cells of the window are read at once, from the location read from (straight from the bucket when no local copy holds the version): this is the way to work with a map too large to read whole. The query takes the same forms as for geospatial data (an sf, sfc or bbox object in any CRS, or H3 cells). A query that does not overlap the raster aborts; one that crosses the antimeridian or holds a pole returns the raster uncropped.

  • Legend. A layer written with categories (see "Rasters" in store_write()) comes back categorical: terra::levels() gives the codes and labels recorded with the dataset, terra::freq() and terra::plot() use the labels, and terra::extract(x, cells, raw = TRUE) gives the codes. The label column is named as it was when the map was written; the code column is named value (code when the label column is itself called value).

  • Colours. A layer written with a colour table has it again: terra::has.colors() is TRUE, terra::coltab() gives the table, and terra::plot() draws with it.

The legend and the colours come from the catalog, not from the file, and nothing is written next to the file. A window and a subset of the layers (x[["name"]]) keep both. There is no columns for rasters: read the raster and take the layers from it.

The location read from is, among the available locations that hold the dataset at the primary's version, a local one first, then the primary, then the other secondaries. Reading from a secondary prints a line saying so (silenced by options(rcs.quiet = TRUE)). Reads use the catalogs held by the connection; store_refresh() reads them again.

Copy to secondary locations

When the primary location is not local (a bucket) and a secondary is a local folder, store_read() first copies the dataset there, so that this read and the next ones come from the local copy. It copies only:

  • to secondaries that are available and local, while the primary is not local: with a local primary, or with secondaries in buckets only, a read copies nothing;

  • the current version, to a secondary that lacks the dataset or its index table, or holds an older version of it. The dataset is copied from the primary with its index table, and only the files the secondary lacks are sent, each verified by its MD5;

  • when the connection's copy_on_read is TRUE (the default of store_connect()) and copy is not FALSE;

  • when the bytes to download, for the secondary that lacks the most, are at or under the limit getOption("rcs.copy_on_read_max_bytes"), 2 GB (2e9) by default. Above it nothing is copied and a message says how to copy (copy = TRUE, or store_sync() with datasets = ).

Filters, columns and intersects do not change the rule: the whole dataset is copied, then read from the copy. A secondary whose version was written later than the primary's is never replaced by a read; a message says so. A secondary that holds the primary's version under another catalog entry (for example a raster written again with another legend or other colours) gets the primary's entry, without any file sent and whatever the limit. A copy that fails gives a warning, and the read goes on from the primary; the next read tries again. Reading an index table never copies; nor do store_sample(), store_glimpse(), store_open() and store_duckdb().

Earlier versions (version = ) are not copied by default. When such a read comes from the primary while an available local secondary could hold a copy, a message says so (unless copying is turned off). copy = TRUE adds the version to the history of each of these secondaries, other than the one it is read from, that holds neither it as its current version nor it in its history: its files, its manifest unchanged, and its rows of the history. With no such secondary at all, a message says there is none to copy to. The secondary's current version of the dataset does not change, and a secondary that does not hold the dataset still does not list it. One effect to know: store_rebuild() of a secondary that holds only an earlier version of a dataset makes that version its current one.

To turn copying off, connect with store_connect(copy_on_read = FALSE), or pass copy = FALSE to one read: nothing is copied and no message about copying is printed (a secondary that already holds the version is still read from). Messages are silenced by options(rcs.quiet = TRUE).

See also

store_open() for lazy queries, store_sample(), store_glimpse().

Examples

location <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-read")
st <- store_connect(location, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(500), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 500 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-read  2/2
#>   files sent  38.3 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
store_read(st, "sales/daily", year == 2023, product == "p07",
  columns = c(shop_id, date, qty)
)
#> # A tibble: 14 × 3
#>    shop_id date         qty
#>      <int> <date>     <int>
#>  1       1 2023-01-22    31

store_write(st, rcs_sim_polygons(200), "shapes/polygons",
  title = "Polygons", description = "Simulated polygons in open ocean."
)

store_read(st, "polygons", intersects = area)

# A class map: whole, and a window of it
if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cover <- terra::as.int(rcs_sim_raster(nrow = 60, ncol = 80)[["cover"]])
  cover[1:2, ] <- 0L
  levels(cover) <- data.frame(
    value = 1:5,
    label = c("water", "forest", "crop", "grass", "bare")
  )
  names(cover) <- "cover"
  terra::coltab(cover) <- data.frame(
    value = 1:5,
    col = c("#1F78B4", "#33A02C", "#FFD92F", "#B2DF8A", "#B15928")
  )
  store_write(st, cover, "grids/cover",
    title = "Land cover", description = "A simulated class map.",
    nodata = 0
  )

  map <- store_read(st, "grids/cover")
  print(map)
  print(terra::levels(map)[[1]]) # the legend
  print(terra::has.colors(map))
  print(terra::coltab(map)[[1]]) # the colours
  print(map[1, 1]) # a cell holding the NoData value is missing

  # Only the cells inside the box of `area`, with legend and colours
  window <- store_read(st, "grids/cover", intersects = area)
  print(dim(window))
  print(terra::freq(window))
  rm(map, window)
}
